summary.name: Being an On-Call Engineer: A Google SRE Perspective
summary.one_liner: A Google research paper describing the principles Google's Site Reliability Engineers use to organize on-call rotations so services stay reliable and the on-call workload stays sustainable.
use_cases: Designing an on-call rotation for an engineering team
Learning how Google SREs organize on-call responsibilities
Keeping services reliable while managing operational load
summary.what_it_does: The page is a summary and abstract of a Google research publication about on-call duty. It states that on-call is a critical responsibility for operations and engineering teams and that organizational pitfalls in rotations and responsibilities can cause serious harm to services and teams. It presents the primary tenets of Google's SRE approach to on-call. It also explains how that approach has produced reliable services and a sustainable workload over time. The page text is only the abstract, so the specific tenets are not listed here.
notable: Describes Google SRE's on-call approach developed over years
Covers pitfalls in on-call rotation and responsibility organization
Published on Google Research as a publication page
caveats: Page text is an abstract only; the full paper's details are not included here
